result.killer: None found. Partial overlap: TRIS (metrology deadlines) and Eco-Himoya cylinder data integration under Res. 315; Res. 325 digitising industrial-safety services; planned oil and gas online-control system (draft due 1 Dec 2026).
result.reason: Nothing I found kills this candidate. The text of Resolution 315 on lex.uz has no small-business exemption. It sets recurring duties: monthly test openings of spring valves, valve checks every 6 months for tanks, metrology verification, periodic vessel inspections and hydraulic tests, signed acts, and staff attestation (stations with uncertified staff are suspended from 1 Jan 2027). Searches in Russian and Uzbek found no private tracker. The state is absorbing parts of the job: TRIS access to calibration deadlines from 1 Sep 2026, linking Eco-Himoya cylinder data, a draft online-control resolution due 1 Dec 2026, and Resolution 325 putting industrial-safety services online. The number of independent owners is unverified. Willingness to pay is doubtful because winter gas limits shut down methane stations. The score stays at 4.

result.killer: Nothing found that kills it outright. Two problems make it unclear: (1) E-mehmon has no public API or bulk import that I could find, so integration would depend on the state's permission or on scraping; (2) the bill raising fines was sent back for revision on 11 Aug 2026 (spot.uz), and its final amounts and start date are not settled. Not checked: the uzinfocom E-mehmon project page returned a 404 error; private connectors for Uzbek PMS users could not be confirmed either way.
result.reason: No named product kills it. Searches in Russian, Uzbek and English found no Uzbek or foreign PMS (Exely, TravelLine, Bnovo, Shelter, 1C) advertising E-mehmon sync, and no public E-mehmon API, import channel or GitHub client. That is the decisive problem: without an official API, a founder would have to scrape the free state portal, which is fragile and may not be allowed. The trigger also weakened. On 11 Aug 2026 the Legislative Chamber sent the higher-fines bill (20-40 BRV, about 8.8-17.6M soums, on officials) back for revision. Deputies objected to the size of the fines and to E-mehmon's own technical failures, and cited a presidential instruction to lower fines on businesses. Officials say all accommodation providers are already connected to E-mehmon, so the tool would only cut manual entry work for the roughly 7,000 accommodation facilities.

result.competitor: The state "Xavfsiz lift" ("Bezopasny lift") single interagency electronic platform of the Ministry of Construction and Housing launched on 1 May (the year was not stated in the results). According to news reports, it offers real-time monitoring of lifts in apartment buildings and holds the electronic register: the Industrial Safety Committee enters new lifts before they are put into use. District khokimiyats enter defects into it, and the cabin plate must show the platform registration number and the last periodic inspection. No private Uzbek lift-compliance software was found.
result.duty: CM resolution No. 431 (12.07.2025) on the technical inspection of lifts, in force 01.07.2026. It requires an inspection by a specialized permitted organization at least once every 12 months, with green/blue/yellow/red marks, and use of red-marked lifts is banned. New lifts must be registered in an electronic system before use. Under the rules for apartment buildings (gov.uz CIRNS, Aug 2026), management bodies must arrange monthly maintenance and annual inspection, keep a lift log and run dispatch supervision. No specific fine amount was found. In Tashkent, 135 people were held administratively liable for industrial-safety violations in general.
result.market: Tashkent has 9,147 lifts in apartment buildings (kun.uz, Nov 2025). The ministry planned inspections for 8,942 lifts in apartment buildings, and a senator cited about 11k lifts across more than 4k apartment buildings. In 2023, 2,422 of 8,857 registered lifts were non-compliant. The number of licensed lift installation and repair firms is listed on the CIRNS (Industrial Safety Committee) site and was not counted here.
result.reason: The duty is real. CM resolution No. 431 of 12.07.2025 requires an inspection by an accredited organization at least every 12 months from 1 July 2026, and red-tagged lifts may not be used. Rules for apartment buildings also require monthly maintenance and a lift log. However, the Construction/Housing Ministry's free interagency "Xavfsiz lift" platform already does the core job. It registers lifts (new lifts can only enter service after registration), stores defects, and its registration number and last inspection date must be shown on the cabin plate. The market is small: about 9-11k lifts in apartment buildings, held by management bodies and khokimiyats. Willingness to pay is low and sales to the public sector are hard. No fine amounts were found.

result.competitor: No private compliance or inspection-readiness tracker for Uzbek stations was found in searches in Russian and Uzbek. Existing tools: U-Gas, the state system for gas-sales monitoring, linked to tax, MVD and Energocontrol, with Eco-Himoya cylinder data to be integrated (not a safety/equipment-life tracker). 1C:KA AZS covers accounting, warehouse and payroll for independent station networks, not safety deadlines. There may be a future risk: Resolution 325 digitises industrial-safety services and permits will use automated-control data from 2027, so state e-services could absorb part of the job. Local expert and inspection firms for pressure vessels exist as a category, but none specific to stations were identified. Benzamat-type pump automation was not confirmed.
result.duty: Confirmed, in force. Uzbekistan Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 315 of 18 June 2026 approved minimum fire, industrial, ecological and process requirements for AZS, AGZS and AGNKS. Annex 3 covers industrial safety: gas pipelines and tanks in good order, safety valves checked at set intervals, automatic overpressure protection on compressors and pumps, and an evacuation plan. Reported document items include a licence, technical passports, working fire equipment, calibrated meters and qualified technical staff. From 1 Sept 2026 to 1 Jan 2030, pressure equipment that is past its service life or has an unknown manufacture date is restricted. Container stations are allowed only as certified modular units. U-Gas is mandatory for AGNKS. A register of violators was due 1 Sept 2026, and a phase-out procedure for above-ground LPG tanks is due 1 Dec 2026. The only penalty found is temporary suspension (464 stations). Fines not found. Oversight sits with the Industrial, Radiation and Nuclear Safety Committee, MChS, Uzenergoinspeksiya and the Ecology Committee. Related: Resolution No. 325 of 25 June 2026 moves industrial-safety state services online, and from 1 Jan 2027 automated control-system data is to be used in permits for hazardous facilities (one gov.uz Uzbek-language source).
result.market: The 2025 inventory covered 6,196 fuel and gas sites (AZS, AGZS, AGNKS and household-cylinder refill points). 1,553 AGNKS are under supervision and registered in U-Gas (1,459 fully connected). The number of small or independent owners versus chains or state-owned stations was not found. The sector is under stress: gas deficits limited methane stations to 6 hours a day in Jan 2026, and no permits for new AGNKS are being issued, per the Deputy PM.
result.reason: The duty is real, new and enforced through suspensions, and no private tracker was found. But the main pain is capital spending (replacing equipment, double-wall tanks, relocation), not paperwork. Recurring tasks like valve checks and service-life dates are simple calendar items. The market is small (about 6,200 sites, about 1,550 AGNKS) and its ownership mix is unknown. Gas shortages are squeezing margins, and the state is digitising industrial-safety services (Resolution 325, automated-control data in permits from 2027). The buyer can be reached through the Committee's outreach events and gas associations. Willingness to pay for software is doubtful. A done-for-you service bundled with expert or inspection firms is the more plausible angle.

result.competitor: The free state portal emehmon.uz has a legal-entity login, and there is a mobile app. Searches in Russian, Uzbek and English found no Uzbek or regional PMS advertising E-mehmon integration. Neither emehmon.uz nor the dgov.uz solution page shows a public API, Excel or bulk import, or connected partners. dgov.uz mentions only automatic transfer to Interior Ministry systems. Kontur.Hotel (Russia) offers a similar API for Russian Interior Ministry guest registration, not for E-mehmon. HSU integration software lists Shelter, Bnovo and 1C Hotel, with no E-mehmon support. Whether Shelter or Bnovo customers in Uzbekistan already have custom E-mehmon connectors was not verified.
result.duty: CM Resolution No. 845 (22 Oct 2018) and No. 433 (2020): accommodation facilities and medical institutions must register foreign citizens and stateless persons in E-mehmon on arrival, for every stay. The system also tracks tourist-fee accruals. A bill tightening liability for failing to register guests or for late E-mehmon entry passed first reading in the Legislative Chamber (103 of 109 votes, reported 22-23 July 2026). Current fine amounts and the Administrative Code article were not found. The bill's final text and effective date were not reached. The 2026 tourist-fee rate was not checked.
result.market: The Statistics Committee counted 1,156 hotels on 1 Jan 2021, led by Tashkent (243), Bukhara (193) and Samarkand (149). The deputy minister cited 1,442 accommodation facilities in 2021, including 210 new hostels. No 2025 count of guest houses was found. Demand is rising: 5.5 million foreign visitors in January-May 2026, up 27% (spot.uz/anhor). Private clinics serving foreign patients add some buyers, but they were not counted. A rough estimate is 2,000-4,000 facilities, not verified.
result.reason: The duty is real. Hotels, motels, sanatoria, guest houses, recreation sites and medical institutions must enter every foreign guest into E-mehmon on arrival (CM Resolutions 845/2018 and 433/2020). A bill raising liability for late or missing E-mehmon entries passed first reading on 23 July 2026; its fine amounts and effective date are unpublished. I found no Uzbek PMS with E-mehmon sync. Neither emehmon.uz nor dgov.uz mentions an API, bulk import or PMS link. dgov.uz describes data transfer only to Interior Ministry systems. That makes the MVP depend on browser automation or a negotiated state integration, which is the decisive risk. Small properties already use the free portal and app. The market is modest: about 1,156 hotels in 2021, plus hostels and guest houses. Buyers are price-sensitive.

result.competitor: No dedicated software or done-for-you service found. Applications go through the free state "Litsenziya" system (license.gov.uz) or my.gov.uz. A June 2026 gov.uz news item confirms this channel for licences in general, but not for the scrap licence specifically. Local lawyers and consultants usually handle one-off licence packs. The Russian-language search for scrap-yard software and Uzbek-language searches turned up no Uzbek vendor.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. The Law of 15 Jan 2026 (lex.uz -7996018, Art. 5) took effect on official publication. It added two licensed activities to the Law on Licensing, Permit and Notification Procedures: procurement, processing and sale of ferrous scrap and waste, and the same for non-ferrous scrap. The licensing body is the Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology, and the state fee is 30 BHM. Cabinet Resolution No. 175 of 16 Apr 2026, reported by UzA on 8 Jul 2026, approved the licensing passports: the documents list, the review procedure, decision deadlines, and licence requirements and conditions. The law sets no transition period. The law's preamble says it abolishes the exclusive rights of large state enterprises. Norma.uz and buxgalter.uz say this means Uzmetkombinat (ferrous) and Uzvtortsvetmet (non-ferrous) lose their monopolies, but I could not open those pages to read it myself. If so, the licence opens a market that was previously closed, and it is not a new burden on existing independent yards. This is mostly a one-off application, followed by ongoing compliance with licence conditions. Not found: the full text of Resolution 175, the specific licence conditions (site, scales, radiation control, CCTV), the licence term, and penalties. The buxgalter.uz answer on sanctions is paywalled.
result.market: Unverifiable. No count of scrap collection points or applicants was found. Until 2026 the trade was legally limited to the networks of the state monopolies Uzmetkombinat and Uzvtortsvetmet. Uzvtortsvetmet was ordered in 2018 to open collection points in every city and district centre. Independent small yards were therefore mostly informal (the claim cites a shadow market of about 500k t/yr). The number of new licensees is likely in the low hundreds and skewed towards mid-size processors, but this is not confirmed.
result.reason: The duty is real: the 15 Jan 2026 law and Resolution 175 of 16 Apr 2026, with a 30 BHM fee and the Ministry of Mining and Geology as the licensing body. However, it is mainly a one-off licence application, submitted free through license.gov.uz or my.gov.uz, and local lawyers can prepare the pack. The licence ends the state monopolies, so it creates market entry rather than a recurring burden on many existing small yards. The number of potential licensees is unknown and probably small. Licence conditions and ongoing reporting duties are unconfirmed. If those duties turn out to be heavy, value could come from ongoing compliance (purchase acts, radiation control, reporting), but that overlaps K03. Low frequency and a narrow market keep the score low.

News (finratings.kz, anhor.uz) reports electronic death certificates from 1 March 2026. It also reports a state "unified electronic register of burial services" module and app, due by 1 June 2026. In a Tashkent pilot from 1 July to 31 Dec 2026, the cemetery head issues burial permits only through the module or app, and paper records end. I found no legal text confirming these dates, and I did not confirm that the register went live. The lex.uz act 1874903 is a 2011 regulation on repatriating remains, not the register. The workflow is entered into the state's own system, by mostly municipal cemetery staff. That makes it the state's own system, so private software has little room. The buyers are few and public, willingness to pay is low, and there is no penalty regime. Mahalla helpers and private funeral firms are not shown to carry a duty. Market size was not found.

result.competitor: State portal my.gov.uz (YaIDXP) for permits and meter registration; state digital systems "Raqamli suv xo'jaligi" and "Suv Hisobi"; no private vendor found
result.duty: Special water-use permit; mandatory registration and sealing of meters on wells and springs from 30 Nov 2025; fines for unpermitted abstraction
result.market: Not quantified; no register figure found
result.reason: Duty is real. The Water Code (ZRU-1076, 30 Jul 2025) took effect 31 Oct 2025. Special water use needs a permit via the state portal (my.gov.uz / YaIDXP). Well meters must be registered and sealed from 30 Nov 2025 (Cabinet Resolution 547). Fines apply per 1000 m3 taken without a permit; the sources I found give 30% of BRV, while the claim says 40%. I did not confirm a daily e-journal. Sources mention only a QR-coded e-act, and the state "Raqamli suv xo'jaligi" and "Suv Hisobi" systems. Those state systems and the portal filing already do the core job, and the duties are mostly one-off, not recurring. Market size is unknown and no register figure was found. Low willingness to pay, and a one-off permit and meter fee is the core cost. Weak SaaS case; at most a done-for-you filing service.

Law 1124 (25 Mar 2026) is confirmed only as administrative liability for illegal removal from collection sites. I could not confirm the 100-300 BRV geo-database fines, the monthly rating, or who files what and how often. The fetched pages (anhor.uz/news/illegal-waste, gov.uz eco 115772) do not mention them. A rating exists: the Agency for Waste Management rates operators green/yellow/red under decree PF-149 (2024). In 2025, 105 operators were rated and 11 fined. So the buyer pool is about 100 firms, many tied to state contracts, and the state runs the monitoring (Tozapoytaxt.uz, 700+ cameras). The duty is mostly state-side and the market is tiny. Few buyers, little recurring filing, so low willingness to pay. Competitor software search not conclusive.

Licensing and personal hallmarks for jewellers are real. Licences come from the State Assay Chamber under the Ministry of Finance, and a 2019 decree moved licensing there. The firms I found keep their own metal records, and I found no mandated record or scrap-log format or periodic filing. Digital labelling of jewellery is only a July 2026 draft: pilot to end-2027, mandatory from 2029 if adopted, and I could not confirm adoption. The state already runs digital licensing and assay services. A small niche with an unconfirmed core duty and no firm count. I ran only 2 searches, so no competitor search for jeweller software and no register count. Score 3.

The duty is real only as a 2024 pilot. Cabinet Resolution No. 44 of 22.01.2024 ran 1 Apr to 1 Oct 2024. Legal entities carrying passengers or freight issue e-waybills themselves, free of charge, in the Ministry of Transport's state "Elektron yo'l varaqa" system (Uztrans). Traffic police and the transport inspectorate check them. Self-employed drivers are excluded. I found no source on whether it became permanent or mandatory after the pilot; no 2025-26 resolution turned up (4 searches, no fetches). No penalty was found. The free state platform already does the core job, and firms issue the waybills themselves, so there is little room for a paid tool. I did not check local fleet-management vendors. No register count of fleets was found. The score is low because of the free state tool and the unclear status.

The yuz.uz article says the reforms are adopted (presidential decree of 5 May 2026) and that from April 2028 the insurance fund may not contract clinics without national or international accreditation. I could not confirm this in the decree text on lex.uz or in a second source. Norma.uz and advice.uz show the decree (PP-170 or PQ-170 and PF-74) but not the 2028 fund rule. The accreditation standards and checklist are not published yet. The duty is a one-off, tied to fund contracts, and the accreditation centre is only now starting. Market is large (9,000+ private clinics, 8.7k expected by end-2026). No competitor found, but the product is still undefined. Weak recurrence and an unclear MVP lead to a low score.
